name: Fanze Meng
intro: I’m an MSc student at Institute of Science Tokyo, working on computational materials in the Tateyama–Ando Lab. My work connects materials science, machine learning, and software for industrial R&D.

projects.title: Material Centre
projects.subtitle: Making materials data easier to explore.
projects.summary: An interactive materials-search application that connects a target property profile with similar polymer grades.
projects.result: Deployed on Volvo’s internal ML platform for user testing and feedback.
projects.problem: Materials selection involves comparing property profiles across many candidate grades. The goal was to give engineers an interactive way to explore materials data and find similar candidates.
projects.contribution: I designed and developed Material Centre, built its similarity-search workflow, and containerised the application for deployment on Volvo’s internal ML platform.
methods: Built an interactive interface with Streamlit and Plotly for exploring property data.
Used principal component analysis and distance metrics to rank similar materials against a target property profile.
Returned the five closest grades and supported comparison of available materials properties and stress–strain curves.
projects.outcome: The application was deployed for internal user testing and feedback. This case study describes the workflow at a high level; the internal application, source code, and industrial datasets are not hosted here.
projects.figure_caption: Conceptual search workflow. This is an original schematic, not a screenshot of the internal application.

projects.title: From microstructure to mechanical response
projects.subtitle: Learning stress–strain behaviour from images.
projects.summary: CNN–Transformer models for stress–strain prediction, with uncertainty estimates and a physics-informed variant.
projects.result: Validation R² = 0.89 on a dataset built from 90 representative volume elements.
projects.problem: Microstructure contains information about a material’s mechanical response. This project explored learning a mapping from microstructure images to tensile stress–strain curves, together with an estimate of predictive uncertainty.
projects.contribution: I designed and developed the prediction models, implemented Monte Carlo dropout for uncertainty estimation, and added a physics-informed model variant.
methods: Combined a ResNet-101 backbone, spatial attention, and a Transformer encoder in PyTorch.
Estimated uncertainty with Monte Carlo dropout.
Added elastic-modulus, smoothness, and boundary-condition losses in a physics-informed variant.
projects.outcome: The model achieved a validation R² of 0.89. This is a validation result rather than a claim of performance on an independent external dataset. The public overview does not include the industrial training data, measured curves, or model weights.
projects.figure_caption: Conceptual model pipeline. The curve is illustrative and does not represent measured data or a model prediction.

projects.title: A smaller set of structures to inspect
projects.subtitle: Graph similarity for 3D electron diffraction.
projects.summary: Clustering crystal-structure candidates to reduce the number requiring manual verification.
projects.result: 97.2% average reduction in candidates requiring manual verification across seven datasets.
projects.problem: Structure solutions from 3D electron diffraction can produce many related candidates. Inspecting each candidate separately creates substantial manual work.
projects.contribution: I built a graph-similarity clustering pipeline for structure candidates and evaluated it across seven experimental datasets containing 2,127 structures.
methods: Represented candidate structures as graphs and compared structural similarity.
Grouped related candidates to reduce the number requiring manual verification.
Also compared Morgan-fingerprint classifiers, including SVM and XGBoost, with a best cross-validated accuracy of 88.7%.
projects.outcome: The clustering workflow reduced the number of structures requiring manual verification by 97.2% on average. This measures a reduction in review workload; it is not a structure-identification accuracy or a guarantee that every correct structure is retained.
projects.figure_caption: Conceptual grouping of related structure candidates. Point counts and positions are schematic, not experimental results.

projects.title: An LLM agent for industrial robot code
projects.subtitle: Connecting technical manuals and code validation.
projects.context: Chalmers University of Technology × Volvo Cars
projects.summary: A proof-of-concept agent for ABB RAPID code generation, grounded in manuals through retrieval-augmented generation.
projects.problem: Generating robot code requires more than translating an instruction into text: the output must follow a specialised language and be evaluated against the intended manufacturing task.
projects.contribution: I co-developed a proof-of-concept LLM agent using the OpenAI GPT API and retrieval over parsed ABB manuals. I implemented an HPC-based framework to validate generated code at scale.
methods: Grounded code generation with retrieval-augmented generation over technical manuals.
Targeted ABB RAPID programs for flexible-manufacturing tasks.
Analysed system performance and scalability with a benchmark of approximately 50 tasks.
projects.outcome: The work established a code-generation and validation workflow. The task count describes benchmark scope; it does not establish a code success rate or certify the safety of generated programs.
projects.figure_caption: Conceptual generation and validation workflow. This is a high-level schematic of the thesis project.
